subject.title: fix(browser): use public ssrf runtime import in CDP proxy bypass

question: Should `registerManagedProxyBrowserCdpBypass` become part of public `openclaw/plugin-sdk/ssrf-runtime`, or should the browser package load path keep using a private owner-scoped helper?
rationale: Current source explicitly keeps this managed-proxy bypass helper private, while this PR assumes it belongs on the public SSRF runtime subpath without adding the export or approval.

options.title: Keep The Helper Private
options.body: Fix the packaged browser import through an owner-scoped private bundled-plugin path and add package smoke coverage without exposing the helper to all plugin consumers.

options.title: Promote To Public SSRF Runtime
options.body: Add the helper to the public `ssrf-runtime` contract with docs, guardrails, and tests that make the new SDK surface intentional.

recommendation.title: Keep The Helper Private
recommendation.body: Fix the packaged browser import through an owner-scoped private bundled-plugin path and add package smoke coverage without exposing the helper to all plugin consumers.

likelyOwner.reason: Kaspre introduced the private SSRF runtime surface and owner-scoped alias coverage that define the boundary this PR touches.
